Source.evidence_source: [/page/14/Text/9] The CDI (Kovacs, 1992) is a 27-item self-report measure of the severity of depressive symptoms. [/page/14/Text/10] The Children's Attributional Style Questionnaire (CASQ; Seligman et al., 1984) is a 48-item forced choice questionnaire that assesses explanatory style for both positive and negative life events. [/page/15/Text/2] The Life Events Questionnaire (LEQ; adapted from Coddington, 1972) is a 24-item checklist of major negative life events that is designed for use with elementary school children. Participants were instructed to check off those events that had happened to them since the previous administration (for the first session it was the past 6 months). [/page/15/Text/3] The following additional questionnaires were also administered at Time 1: The CPIC (Grych et al., 1992) and the CCQ (Loranger & Arsenault, 1989). Demographic information such as parental education and family income were collected from children and their parents. Finally, children's academic reports (grades) were obtained from their teachers.
